description_original: In this exercise you will write some functions which can be used in games that involve dice. Instead of normal dice this exercise specifies _non-transitive dice_. You can read up on these [here](https://singingbanana.com/dice/article.htm) or [watch this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LrIp6CKUlH8). You will use three dice: - Die A has the sides 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 6 - Die B has the sides 2, 2, 2, 5, 5, 5 - Die C has the sides 1, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4 Please write a function named `roll(die: str)`, which rolls the die specified by the argument. An example of how this should work: ```python for i in range(20): print(roll("A"), " ", end="") print() for i in range(20): print(roll("B"), " ", end="") print() for i in range(20): print(roll("C"), " ", end="") ``` 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 6 3 6 3 2 2 5 2 2 5 5 2 2 5 2 5 5 5 2 5 2 2 2 2 4 4 4 4 4 1 1 4 4 4 1 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 Also write a function named `play(die1: str, die2: str, times: int)`, which throws both dice as many times as specified by the third argument. The function should return a tuple. The first item should be the number of times die 1 won, the second the number of times die 2 won, and the third item should be the number of ties. ```python result = play("A", "C", 1000) print(result) result = play("B", "B", 1000) print(result) ``` (292, 708, 0) (249, 273, 478)
